privateLongRunObservation: Pinned 60-million-step Windows A/B used the pre-rebase CLI SHA-256 01342af139cd84727c7eb4d4a6b36f6acfe88878b92da20d65f550413f6dfd41. Its normalized guest report matched ordinary stepping, including CPU, serial, text, VGA, events and inputs. Ordinary cost 78.40 user CPU seconds versus 295.91 for opt-in (3.77x slower); 2,730,404 native instructions (4.55%) in 1,263,367 calls (mean 2.16), with 57,269,596 fallbacks. The final CLI adds the unrelated mode CPU profiler option and rejects concurrent profiling; the long-run timing is not attributed to its changed CLI bytes. Raw reports and commercial media remain private.
limitations: Exact-address read proof exits if prior instructions change an EA register. This option is disabled by default and should not be used for performance; the measured opt-in was 3.77x slower in user CPU time.
